summary: Checklist ownership was unclear after a synthetic discharge transition.

established_facts: Synthetic handoff timestamp preceded the receiving shift change.
The checklist has no explicit receiving-role field in this scenario.
hypotheses: A single assigned role may reduce queue ambiguity.
open_questions: Would a single queue add duplicate documentation?
How should a resident's preferred communication format be carried forward?
five_whys: No owner was visible in the handoff.
The form did not require a receiving role.
The workflow has no shared role-to-queue standard.
findings: Human-authored working finding: role ambiguity is a testable systems contributor; not a definitive root cause.

summary: Two synthetic transition records contained different medication-list versions.

hypotheses: Version labeling could improve reconciliation visibility.
